title: Cephalometric X-ray for the orthodontist
what: This is a picture of the head from the side. From it, the orthodontist measures the position of the jaws and teeth.
why: Before braces or aligners, to plan orthodontic treatment, and to check the result.
duration: the picture itself takes a few seconds, the whole visit usually 5 to 10 minutes; the picture is usually handed over right away
tell_doctor: Pregnancy, or if it is possible
If you have braces, piercings, or removable dentures
If a child finds it hard to stand still, tell the staff beforehand

prepare.title: Jewelry
prepare.text: Take off earrings, hairpins, glasses, and any piercings on the head and neck.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: No metal around the neck and shoulders.

steps: A protective apron is put on you
You stand or sit at the machine
Your head is held by soft supports at the ears
You are asked to close your teeth and not move
For a few seconds, the machine takes the picture
feel: The ear supports may press a little
after: You can go about your usual day right away
The picture is usually handed over right away or sent to your orthodontist
The orthodontist will explain the measurements and treatment plan at the visit

faq.q: Is it harmful for a child?
faq.a: The radiation dose is small. The picture is taken only when it is needed for treatment.

faq.q: How is it different from a panoramic X-ray?
faq.a: A panoramic picture shows all the teeth. This one shows the head from the side, to measure jaw position.

reminders.text: Cephalometric X-ray in 2 hours. Take off earrings and hairpins, and bring the orthodontist's referral.
